title: Buyer and supplier e-mails make claims that are not always true
evidence: shared/orchestration/matchmaking.py:609 indicative offer says 'supplied by a GST- and IEC-verified Indian manufacturer' and 'the pre-shipment inspection by the agency you choose' — the pair's supplier may be unverified (matchmaking.py:324-327 only lowers reliability to 0.8 when GST/IEC are unknown) and only QIMA can be booked (qc_providers.py:959 QC_PROVIDERS_ENABLED default qima); shared/company_profile.py:113 tells suppliers 'Buyers who receive a good first shipment reorder through us' (a track record PortLess does not have yet) and :110 'you deliver FOB Indian port' while manual EXW suppliers are collected by PortLess
impact: A buyer who later learns the supplier was not verified, or that it could not choose the inspector, has a misrepresentation argument at the first dispute; company_profile's own rule is 'only true-by-design statements'
fix: Say 'verified' only when the pair's supplier has gst_verified and iec_active True (else 'a manufacturer we verify before the order'); name the inspector actually bookable ('an independent inspector (QIMA)'); drop the reorder sentence; say 'FOB Indian port or ex-works' for suppliers
why_money: no dispute lost on a sentence PortLess wrote itself
